nodes.body: When lowering `iand(x, (2^n-1))` to `umod(x, 2^n)`, building the modulus with `nir_imm_intN_t(..., alu->def.bit_size)` truncates `2^n` when `n == bit_size` (e.g., 8-bit mask 0xff -> modulus 256 -> becomes 0 in 8-bit). That turns an identity mask into `umod(x, 0)` (which NIR treats as 0), changing semantics from `x` to `0`. Treat the full-width mask case as an identity lane (emit `nir_channel(x, component)`) and skip the exact-integer-window check for that lane.

The new scalar bit-size regression only checks masks where (mask+1) fits in the destination bit size (e.g., 7->8). To guard against the truncation edge case that motivated this PR, it would help to add cases for full-width masks (e.g., 8-bit 0xff and 16-bit 0xffff) and assert they lower to an identity (no `umod`, no rejection) rather than accidentally producing a zero-divisor path.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep full-width 8/16-bit masks from becoming modulo zero**

When `alu->def.bit_size` is 8 or 16 and the constant mask covers every bit (`0xff` or `0xffff`), the validation above accepts it because `moduli[component]` becomes `256` or `65536`, a power of two within the FP24 exact window. Passing that value to `nir_imm_intN_t` with the narrow result bit size truncates the divisor to zero, so `x & 0xff`/`x & 0xffff` lowers to `umod x, 0`, which `nir_lower_int_to_float` treats as zero instead of the identity value.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep shadow planner cut selection in sync**

When the first transport-valid cut's halves fail to compile but a later ranked cut succeeds, this loop records the failure and keeps walking until it can return `SPLIT`. The live admission and delivery paths still use `r300_mp_find_vec4_cut()` in `r300_r2vb_split_admitted()` / `r300_r2vb_run_split_producer()`, which selects only the first transport-valid cut and never tries the later one, so with `R300_R2VB_BUDGET_ESCAPE=spill1` the memo can reject while the shadow plan reports split and trips the new parity assert. Either the live splitter needs to use the same selected candidate as the planner, or the shadow plan must mirror the single-candidate behavior until it becomes authoritative.

Measuring the clone here without that optimize step makes the emitted selected-phase stats describe a different, dead-code-containing program than the row's plan cost vectors and the real producer path, so the mining output can disagree with the selected plan even while the census passes.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require stats from each selected split half**

For SPLIT rows this checks only the aggregate `selected_stats`, so if one selected half emits no `SHADER_INFO` line because its recompilation rejects or stops before stats while the other half emits normally, the row still passes and the mining transcript silently lacks `selected-pass-a` or `selected-pass-b`. Since the header makes both selected halves the mining surface, the census should assert a nonzero stats count for each expected phase rather than only the sum.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject fractional FP classes in the source-domain test**

When this predicate is implemented as written, a `b2i32`-derived carry does not decline: `nir_analyze_fp_class` sets `FP_CLASS_POS_ZERO | FP_CLASS_GT_ZERO_LT_POS_ONE` for `nir_op_b2i*` in `src/compiler/nir/nir_range_analysis.c:857-865`, so the mask has `FP_CLASS_NON_INTEGRAL`, NaN, and inf clear. Because the documented test only excludes those bits and says `b2i` keeps `NON_INTEGRAL` set, a bit-reinterpreted 1 can satisfy the integral obligation and be admitted as an exact FP24 integer; add an explicit fractional-class/non-float-output rejection or fix the design before implementing it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Base the boolean floor on the fragment lowering**

For the restaged producer path, `r300_r2vb_build_restaged_fs_nir` marks the clone as `MESA_SHADER_FRAGMENT` (`src/gallium/drivers/r300/r300_r2vb.c:619-622`), so `r300_optimize_nir` runs `r300_nir_lower_bool_to_float_fs`, not the VS `r300_nir_lower_bool_to_float`. That FS algebraic pass rewrites `b2f32(compare)` to `fcsel_ge(...)` (`src/gallium/drivers/r300/compiler/r300_nir_algebraic.py:181-187`), and `nir_analyze_fp_class` has no `fcsel_ge` case, so boolean compares become `FP_CLASS_UNKNOWN` rather than the provable `{0,1}` class described here. An implementation following this will fail the advertised boolean T0/T1 admission floor until the range engine or pass boundary handles the actual lowered shape.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Prove the original conversion source**

For a carried value like `f2i32(load_input)` that is clamped before transport, checking the later `i2f32`/`u2f32` transport result proves only that the already-converted integer is integral; it does not prove that the original float input converted to the same integer on the FP24 producer and the software vertex reference. The preceding section identifies exactly this quantization-before-`f2i` divergence, so an implementation following this wording can admit fractional sources near an integer boundary as soon as the post-conversion integer is range-bounded; the predicate needs to chase and prove the float operand of `f2i32`/`f2u32`, or decline.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep system values out of the proved floor**

The producer plan does not currently prove or admit this sysval class: `r300_r2vb_plan.c` only allows plain I/O plus uniform/UBO/push/constant intrinsics and returns `R300_R2VB_PLAN_INTRINSIC` for other intrinsics, and `r300_r2vb_plan_oracle_test.c` has `load_vertex_id` expecting that reject. The default synthetic sysval path is a float `load_deref` input rather than a `nir_i2f32` definition, so listing “float-encoded integer system values” as proved today will make the implementation or oracle expect an admission path that the current route explicitly rejects.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

_🎯 Functional Correctness_ | _🟠 Major_ | _🏗️ Heavy lift_

**Restrict integer-origin admission to operations with proven path identity.**

Bounding every intermediate to `+-2^17` is insufficient for generic “integer ALU”: it proves exact representation of values, not that every NIR operation and its FP24 lowering matches the FP32 reference. Define an explicit supported-operation whitelist, or require an operation-level lowering proof; unsupported or unmodeled integer operations must decline rather than pass on range bounds alone.

<details>
<summary>Proposed wording</summary>

```diff
-   value, or contract-seeded integer attribute flowing through integer ALU
-   whose every intermediate is proven inside the `+-2^17` window
+   value, or contract-seeded integer attribute flowing only through an
+   explicitly supported integer operation whose FP24 lowering is proven
+   path-identical, with every intermediate inside the `+-2^17` window
```
</details>
